source.title: The Mathematical Theory of Double Descent as Shrinkage, not Overfitting: Matching Bounds for Path-Regularized Multilayer Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations have formatting or extraction artifacts, but the document is readable and not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves width-wise double descent results for a path-regularized estimator and refines the proposed mechanism, arguing that the rise is caused by shrinkage rather than overfitting. It does not empirically reproduce the original unregularized settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds and claims about the estimator’s error, not numerical experiments. Cited empirical findings and values used only in derivations to set the regularization schedule are not separate outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proves, for path-regularized multilayer networks under a width-regime regularization schedule, matching upper and lower bounds. These show the error descends, peaks near the interpolation threshold δn=1 and descends again (Theorem XI.3). It also argues that the ascent comes from required shrinkage, not variance or noise fitting (Theorem XI.5). This is a specific theoretical result bearing on V1 and on V6's mechanism. There are no experiments, and the setting is not the original unregularized training.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. For the path-regularized estimator and its regime-wise schedule, the error itself, not just a bound, descends, rises to a peak at δn=1 whose height does not shrink with n, and descends again. The ascent is shrinkage required by the underparameterized regularization, not overfitting. No width-independent λ that keeps the theory's guarantees removes it. The authors explicitly do not claim this mechanism explains double descent in unregularized training, nor that error-optimal per-width tuning would keep the peak.
record.recipe_differences: Nonasymptotic theoretical analysis of PeSV/path-regularized empirical risk minimization with width-regime-specific regularization; no empirical sweep, and not the original unregularized experimental method.
record.method_sensitivity: The curve depends on the regime-wise regularization schedule and the width threshold δₙ=1. The population-error peak bound additionally depends on target spread/coherence and the stated signal-to-noise condition.
record.problems: No numerical or empirical validation is reported. The population-error peak requires extra target/signal conditions; the unconditional peak result is for empirical error. The mechanism is explicitly limited to the path-regularized estimator, not unregularized training.
record.rows_left_out: None; the paper reports no separate numerical experiments on the claim.

untested.parts: Unregularized or SGD-trained networks; any empirical width sweep. The result holds only for the PeSV/path-regularized ERM with the prescribed λ schedule.
Sample-size sweeps near the threshold; not studied.
Other model classes; only conjectured that the argument extends.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peaks across axes. δn is used only along the width axis.
Triple or multiple descent; whether error-optimal, per-width tuned regularization removes the peak (explicitly not claimed); explicit label-noise sweeps.
Replotting against an effective parameter count. The paper only remarks that weight count is not the right complexity measure.

missing.what: Upper-bound analysis: whether the second valley (plateau) lies below the first (U-bottom) depends on the signal-to-noise ratio ||f*||²/σϵ² exceeding a threshold (B≥A), and on the specific choice f(n)=n^((β−1)/(β+1))(log n)^(2/(β+1)).
missing.locator: Section X, discussion after Theorem X.1, Eq. (53); Remark VII.1.1

missing.what: Shape of the error floor Fl(m) across four phases (first descent, valley, ascent to min{||f*||ₙ,(C1σϵ−ξ)/Lσ^(L−1)}, drop at δn=1 then decrease), matching the upper bound's shape.

record.verdict_notes: Purely theoretical; no numerical curves. The peak is tied to a prescribed width-dependent λ, with a discontinuity at δn=1, so the support for V1 is conditional on that estimator. r7 state changed from reversed to partial because the noise level still controls peak height. The V6 label for r8 was dropped because the row does not address optimally tuned regularization. Lower bounds are per-target, with constants depending on ρ(f*), and are not uniform over the target ball.

versions.untested_parts: No empirical model-size sweep or unregularized-training setting; the result is for path-regularized multilayer networks with a prescribed width-dependent schedule.
Training time or epoch-wise error curves.
A sample-size sweep measuring whether increasing training samples raises test error near the interpolation threshold.
Tests on other model classes; possible extensions are proposed but not established by results.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Triple or multiple peaks and whether independently error-optimizing, width-specific regularization removes the peak; the paper explicitly does not claim that such tuning must produce a peak.
Replotting or measuring the second descent against an effective parameter count to determine whether it becomes an ordinary U-curve.

rows.subject: path-regularized multilayer fully connected neural network estimator g(·; θ̂)
rows.size_stated: Width vector m; no numerical widths stated.

rows.operation_detail: Bound the estimation error conditional on the regularization exceeding the empirical noise-process term.
rows.measure: Upper bound on ||g(·; θ̂)−f*||ₙ² and whether it contains a variance term
rows.value: The bound is C₁H(m)²||f*||²_WL+4λ||f*||_WL and contains neither a number-of-weights term nor a σϵ²/n variance term; the authors attribute the ascent to width-dependent shrinkage rather than noise fitting.
rows.uncertainty: The theorem is stated conditional on λ≥ξ; no separate probability level is given for this inequality.
rows.locator: Section XI.F, Theorem XI.5 and Remark XI.5.1, Eq. (83)
rows.note: This result challenges the noise/variance-driven account for the studied path-regularized estimator; the authors explicitly do not extend this mechanism claim to unregularized training.
rows.check: Not 'reversed'. Theorem XI.5's bound has no σϵ²·(weights)/n variance term, so the variance/overfitting route is absent. But noise still sets the peak height through the schedule: Fl♯ contains C1σϵ, so the peak vanishes as σϵ→0. The noise-dependence part holds; the variance mechanism does not.
